extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and reviewers involved in systematic reviews and evaluations of large language models (LLMs) in health care; journal editors and guideline developers
extracted.subtask_short: critique systematic reviews of medical LLMs
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying methodological, conceptual, and reporting limitations in systematic reviews of large language models applied to health care, to improve clinical applicability and methodological rigor. The page is a journal letter pointing out specific weaknesses in a clinician-focused review of LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation Threshold Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors exclude journals below a citation threshold of 13,000, which introduces a publication bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding low-citation or newer/specialized journals risks omitting innovative research; in rapidly evolving fields, important innovations may first appear in newer venues. Reviews should avoid arbitrary citation cutoffs or otherwise account for the exclusion's effects on findings and the prevalence of negative results (the authors note only 8.9% reported negative results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flawed Performance Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of “best performance” is problematic because performance level in one context does not guarantee similar performance in different contexts; thus frequency of “best performance” should not be interpreted as a metric for comparing models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using a single, context-insensitive frequency metric to compare models. Account explicitly for heterogeneity in evaluation metrics, datasets, and contexts across studies; recognize that such heterogeneity renders simple performance comparisons misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Quality Assessment of Included Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The review lacks assessment of the included studies (study design, validation approaches, statistical rigor) and instead simply counts “best performance” instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews should evaluate study quality (design, sample sizes, validation methodology, statistical rigor) rather than aggregating superficial performance counts. Use established quality assessment tools and weigh findings by methodological robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual and Analytical Oversimplification
rubrics_metrics.description: The 5-stage linear workflow model oversimplifies the complex and iterative nature of clinical decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer conceptual models that capture parallel processes, feedback loops, and multidisciplinary coordination present in modern health care. Analytical frameworks should reflect complexity of implementation rather than imposing linear workflows that limit practical utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient Discussion of Clinical Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The review inadequately addresses the critical gap between research performance and clinical validation; models trained and validated on research datasets often face substantial deployment challenges in medical institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews should weigh external and real-world validation evidence heavily, discuss generalizability and dataset–setting differences, and explicitly assess deployment-readiness and barriers to clinical integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Safety and Risk Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Although ethical concerns are discussed, the analysis of patient safety is superficial and lacks comprehensive risk assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include thorough safety and risk analyses covering failure modes, error propagation, and impacts on clinical decision-making. Reviews should synthesize literature on harms, mitigation strategies, and safety monitoring relevant to implementing medical AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of Economic Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The review lacks a comprehensive economic evaluation of LLM implementation, including cost-effectiveness, resource allocation, and return-on-investment assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments of clinical applicability should include economic analyses (cost-effectiveness, resource implications, ROI) because economic factors materially affect feasibility and adoption in clinical settings.
